subject: Re: CAIQ claim synthesis & ownership playbook for LumenBridge
messages:
From: Matt Chen <matt.chen@lumenbridge.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: security-audit <audit@lumenbridge.com>
Date: 2027-06-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: CAIQ: Clarify control claim for tenant isolation / evidence ask

Hi Kimberly / Jonas,

Thanks for sending the initial CAIQ response file earlier. Our audit team has a couple of follow-ups before we can sign off on the tenant isolation assertions (CCM.SI-01 / CCM.SI-04 area). Specifically:

- Can you confirm which runtime variant (hosted vs dedicated) the claim applies to? The questionnaire has an assertion that reads "customer tenant data is logically isolated across hosted and dedicated deployments" — we need to see how that differs for private deployments.
- Request for a small set of runtime telemetry showing tenant-id separation across a sample day (anonymized). A csv or text snippet with timestamps + tenant-id hashed is fine.
- Who is the control owner we should list for on-going evidence requests? We need an email contact for the attestation log.

Deadline: our compliance window for review is 2027-07-05. If you can get back with the clarified assertion text and a sample telemetry extract it would help speed validation.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to hop on a 30-min call if that helps.

Best,
Matt
Principal Security Engineer
LumenBridge

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Matt Chen <matt.chen@lumenbridge.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-26T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ: Clarify control claim for tenant isolation / evidence ask

Matt — thanks for the clear list. We can provide a concise, claim-level justification and the telemetry sample. High-level plan below:

1) Claim scoping text (draft attached) — we will call out three scoped variants: Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved capacity), Private (VPC/on-prem). The assertion language will be explicit about logical isolation guarantees vs operational differences (e.g., customer-managed network for Private).
2) Evidence sample — attached: runtime-telemetry-snippet.txt (anonymized, tenant-hash + timestamp + routing node).
3) Control owner — brief roster attached (ownership-roster.csv) with primary contact and secondary.

I've attached a working workbook (caiq-claim-draft.xlsx) with a proposed mapping row for CCM.SI-01 / CCM.SI-04 and suggested owner and evidence pointers. Jonas, can you review the proposed wording on the mapping tab and confirm the evidence pointer for the hosted runtime? Marissa, can you confirm the KMS/HSM pointer we'd include for Private deployment variants?

If you'd prefer a call, I have availability tomorrow between 9:30–11:00 PT. Otherwise we'll update the sheet and circulate a one-pager for your audit team.

Attachments: caiq-claim-draft.xlsx (spreadsheet - draft mapping), runtime-telemetry-snippet.txt (anonymized sample), ownership-roster.csv (contacts)

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Matt Chen <matt.chen@lumenbridge.com>
Date: 2027-06-27T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ: Clarify control claim for tenant isolation / evidence ask

On Sat, Jun 26, 2027 at 09:12 AM Matt Chen <matt.chen@lumenbridge.com> wrote:
> Thanks for sending the initial CAIQ response file earlier. Our audit team has a couple of follow-ups before we can sign off on the tenant isolation assertions...

Thanks Matt — quick notes after I reviewed kimberly's draft mapping:

- Hosted vs Dedicated: the logical isolation claim is identical at the application layer (same multitenant service), but Dedicated includes config-level tenant affinity (reserved GPU pools) and export controls; I updated the mapping cell to call this out.
- Private: changed the wording to read: "Private deployments (VPC/on‑prem) rely on customer-managed network controls and may require customer attestation for physical/host-level separation." That makes the boundary explicit.
- Evidence pointer for hosted runtime: I added a link to the telemetry snippet and a short note that prefix/KV cache partitioning is enforced per-tenant (see row 14).

Action items I completed in the workbook:
• Updated claim language (Mapping tab, row 4)
• Added telemetry field descriptions (Evidence tab)

Kimberly / Marissa: please review my edits; if green I'll export the minimal evidence package for LumenBridge (redacted as needed). Matt — if you want a short walkthrough of the workbook, I can do 20 minutes Monday morning.

-Jonas
Director, Applied ML Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Matt Chen <matt.chen@lumenbridge.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-29T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ: Clarify control claim for tenant isolation / evidence ask

Matt, Kimberly, Jonas —

We pulled the final artifacts together and staged an intake bundle in the shared Drive. Contents:
- CAIQ mapping sheet (finalized wording + owner column) — caiq-claim-draft.xlsx
- Telemetry sample (anonymized, hashed tenant ids) — runtime-telemetry-snippet.txt
- Ownership roster with operational contacts — ownership-roster.csv

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_LumenBridge-CAIQ
Doc notes: the CAIQ mapping includes a short narrative per claim to help auditors reconcile the assertion vs evidence.

Planned next steps:
1) Kimberly to share a 1-page attestation summary we can include in the submission (ETA: tomorrow EOD).
2) Jonas to produce a sanitized log export if the auditor requests additional slices (will require two business days).
3) Marissa (me) will coordinate any DocuSign acceptance or formal attestation paperwork.

If LumenBridge audit wants a Zoom walkthrough, propose Tue 2027-07-01 09:00 PT and we'll confirm.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Sr. Technical Program Manager, Compliance
Redwood Inference
